Application Materials.content:
The application portal will prompt you to upload your application documents online. Preferably, you can upload all your documents in PDF format. Please ensure that scanned documents are clear and legible. Failure to do so will result in delays to the processing of your application.
1. Personal Identification Document
- NRIC Identity Card (for Singapore Citizens)
- Passport, Blue NRIC Identity Card and Re-entry Permit (for Singapore Permanent Residents)
- Passport and Employment Pass or Dependent Pass (for non-Singaporeans applying for part-time programme)
- Passport (for non-Singapore Citizens)
2. Degree Scroll and Official Transcript from each University attended (with English translation if applicable)
3. GMAT / GRE / SMU Admission Test Score Report
4. IELTS / TOEFL (required if your degree was not taught in English)
5. Updated Resume
6. Personal Statement
7. Two Referee Reports
Both your referees will receive an auto-generated email to complete an online referee report upon the submission of your online application. You can monitor referee report submission status via the [Applicant Self Service](https://eservices.smu.edu.sg/psp/ps/?cmd=login) portal.
If you would like to submit additional documents (e.g., latest academic transcript, new test results, etc.) after the submission of your online application, you may send them to us separately via email: [msfe@smu.edu.sg](mailto:msfe@smu.edu.sg).
Admission requirements include: Personal statement, Updated resume, and References (2).

Interview Requirements.content:
- Shortlisted applicants with complete application records will be contacted for admission interview.
- Admission Requirements include: Admission Interview.
- Shortlisted applicants will be invited for an interview. For international students, interviews will be conducted via Zoom if they are not in Singapore.

Academic Requirements.content:
- **Good Bachelor's degree**.
- Applicants must demonstrate **good prior academic performance in an undergraduate degree from a recognised institution of higher learning**.
- The August intake will now be open to students from **diverse academic backgrounds**. Foundation courses will be provided to bridge any knowledge gaps. Students with **strong quantitative backgrounds** may be exempted from these courses and complete the programme in 12 months.
- The programme welcomes **applicants from all disciplines**, including those who may not have prior exposure to economic theory or quantitative techniques. Students who demonstrate **substantial knowledge in economics and quantitative techniques** may be granted exemptions from foundational courses.
- There are two admission pathways: the **Accelerated Pathway** is for students with **strong economics/finance knowledge and quantitative techniques** who are exempted from foundation courses; the **Regular Pathway** is for students from other disciplines who do not have the necessary training in economics theory, finance and quantitative techniques.
- UG CGPA may be used in place of GRE/GMAT/SMU Admission Test scores for: **SMU alumni with CGPA 3.0/4.0 or above, within five years of graduation**; **NUS/NTU/SUTD/SUSS/SIT alumni with CGPA 3.5/5.0 or above, within five years of graduation**. Meeting the CGPA academic criteria listed above does not guarantee admission.

GRE GMAT Requirements.content:
- Application documents include **GMAT / GRE / SMU Admission Test Score Report**.
- Admission requirements include a **good score in GMAT/GRE/SMU Admission Test**. **UG CGPA may be used in place of GRE/GMAT/SMU Admission Test scores** for the following applicants:
- **SMU alumni with CGPA 3.0/4.0 or above, within five years of graduation.**
- **NUS/NTU/SUTD/SUSS/SIT alumni with CGPA 3.5/5.0 or above, within five years of graduation.**
- _Note: Meeting the CGPA academic criteria listed above does not guarantee admission, and you may be advised to submit your GMAT/GRE/SMU Admission Test score to improve your chances of admission._
- The GMAT/GRE is recommended. However, if you have not taken the GMAT or GRE test, you may consider taking the online SMU Admission Test, which comprises three components: verbal, numerical, and inductive reasoning. Please click [Fact Sheet](https://economics.smu.edu.sg/sites/economics.smu.edu.sg/files/economics/MSFE/SMU%20Admission%20Test%20Fact%20sheet%20%28MSFE%29.pdf) for information on SMU Admission Test registration and test details.
- If you intend to take the SMU Admission Test, please proceed to complete the MSFE application first and make a payment of **S$125** in addition to the MSE application fee of **S$100**. Once you have completed payment for the test, send an email with your full name, application number and payment receipt to [msfe@smu.edu.sg](mailto:msfe@smu.edu.sg).
- FAQ admission requirements state: **GMAT or GRE or SMU Admission Test** is a compulsory requirement for admission to this programme. Candidates may only take the SMU Admission Test after they have submitted the online application form.
- For GMAT, scores **600 or above** are sought. For GRE, the verbal plus quantitative average should be **156 or above**. For SMU Admissions Test, the Verbal/Numerical/Integrated Reasoning average should be **55 or above**. These are not hard cut-offs; the programme looks at the overall application and can accept students who fall below one or more of these minimums if there are positives in the application that compensate. Only one of GRE/GMAT/SMUAT is needed.
- GMAT scores are valid for **5 years** after the test date. If GMAT results are older than **5 years**, applicants need to re-sit GMAT.
- For most applicants, GRE/GMAT is required. UG CGPA may be used in place of GRE/GMAT/SMU Admission Test scores for SMU alumni with CGPA **3.0/4.0 or above, within 5 years of graduation**, and NUS/NTU/SUTD/SUSS/SIT alumni with CGPA **3.5/5.0 or above, within 5 years of graduation**. Meeting these CGPA criteria does not guarantee admission, and candidates may be recommended to submit GMAT/GRE/SMU Admission Test scores if it is felt this would improve chances of admission.

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
- IELTS / TOEFL is **required if your degree was not taught in English**.
- Admission requirements include a **good TOEFL or IELTS (required if your first degree was not taught in English)**.
- Applicants must show proficiency in English language. A TOEFL or IELTS test is required if the applicant's undergraduate degree was not conducted in English.
- For TOEFL and IELTS, your score should be **90 / 6.5 or above**. These are not hard cut-offs; the programme looks at the overall application and can accept students who fall below one or more minimums if there are positives in the application that compensate. TOEFL or IELTS is required only if your first degree is not in English.
- TOEFL scores are valid for **2 years** after the test date.
- All lessons and examinations are conducted in English for both pathways under the MSFE programme.

Program Overview.content:
- The Master of Science in Financial Economics (MSFE) programme combines two central strengths of SMU – econometrics and finance – in a programme that meets the industry demand for professionals with the skills for deep analysis of increasingly complex financial problems in a new era of dynamic policy and regulation. Students learn how modelling, forecasting and surveillance methods developed in financial theory and econometrics address industry challenges. The programme is for students who seek to pursue a career in the finance industry or research.
- The MSFE is a rigorous multi-disciplinary programme that gives students in-depth understanding of financial markets and their interaction with the macroeconomy, backed by strong econometrics training for analysing economic and financial data. It offers two intakes annually, January and August, and caters to both full-time and part-time students.
- Duration: 18 months full-time, with flexibility to complete in 12 months; 30 months part-time, with flexibility to complete in 24 months. The maximum candidature is 2.5 years for full-time students and 4 years for part-time students.
- The programme welcomes applicants from all disciplines, including those who may not have prior exposure to economic theory or quantitative techniques. Students who demonstrate substantial knowledge in economics and quantitative techniques may be granted exemptions from foundational courses. Effective August 2026, foundation courses will be provided to bridge knowledge gaps, while students with strong quantitative backgrounds may be exempted and complete the programme in 12 months through the accelerated pathway, available in both August and January intakes.
- The MSFE is a 15 course unit (CU) programme, available for full-time study with internship opportunities. Its structure comprises Foundation, Core, Elective, Open, and Postgraduate Professional Development components. Effective August 2026, the Foundation component will be reduced from 4 CUs to 3 CUs and the Open component increased from 1 CU to 2 CUs, allowing more flexibility and personalization while maintaining a strong academic foundation.
- Full-time students are required to complete a minimum 10-week internship during the April Term. If unable to take a credit-bearing internship, students may seek approval to arrange an equivalent replacement, such as a Capstone Project or electives. Students with two years of relevant work experience by graduation may be exempted from the internship requirement, subject to approval.
- The programme is multidisciplinary, delivering economics, econometrics and financial theory; it teaches advanced tools of economic theory, financial econometrics and statistical computation; and it aims to equip students with fundamentals to anticipate and handle future financial crises. Students learn from econometricians, qualified and experienced faculty members and industry practitioners.
- Class profile: typical age range 25 years; gender profile 49(M) : 51(F), based on Classes of 2018-2021 full-time student profiles.
- Industries MSFE graduates work in: Financial Services 50%, Government 14%, Technology 9%, Education 9%, Consulting 5%, Real Estate 5%, Audit / Accounting 4%, Manufacturing 4%, based on Classes of 2018-2020 full-time student data.
- MSFE is a Masters Degree programme at SMU by coursework, also called a Professional Masters Program. There are no thesis requirements.
- All lessons and examinations are conducted in English for both pathways under the MSFE programme.
- SMU has an internal online job portal for students to search and apply for internships and jobs. Students are assigned a dedicated career coach to provide career advisory and prepare them for internship and job placement.

Curriculum.content:
#### Programme Structure
The Master of Science in Financial Economics (MSFE) programme offers two intakes annually (January and August), catering to both full-time and part-time students. August, January and April are regular 10-week terms. November and July are optional 5-week terms.
- **18 Months Full-Time** with flexibility to complete in **12 months**.
- **30 Months Part-Time** with flexibility to complete in **24 months**.
- The maximum candidature is **2.5 years for full-time students** and **4 years for part-time students**.
- Part-time students typically take **1-3 CUs per regular term** (Aug, Jan, Apr), whereas full-time students take **2-5 CUs**.
- The MSFE is a **15 course unit (CU)** programme, available for full-time study with internship opportunities.
- Each course unit (CU) comprises **ten 3-hour sessions**.
- Graduation requires a Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA) of at least **2.50 on a 4.00 scale**.
Current curriculum structure:
| Component | Course Units |
| --- | --- |
| Foundation | 4CUs |
| Core | 6CUs |
| Elective | 3CUs |
| Open | 1CU |
| PGPD | 1CU |
The curriculum structure will be updated effective August 2026:
| Component | Course Units |
| --- | --- |
| Foundation | 3CUs |
| Core | 6CUs |
| Elective | 3CUs |
| Open | 2CUs |
| PGPD | 1CU |
**Foundation (4CUs)**: The Foundation component provides essential training in economic theory and advanced quantitative methods. Choose four: Principles of Economics 1, Principles of Economics 2, Mathematics for Economics, Further Mathematics for Economics. The Foundation component will be streamlined to **3CU effective August 2026**, comprising: Principles of Economics, Statistical Inference, Mathematics for Economics.
**Core (6CUs)**: Corporate Finance; Econometric Analysis; Empirical Finance; Financial Econometrics; Macroeconomic Analysis; Microeconomic Analysis.
**Elective (3CUs)**: Students have the flexibility to choose 3 elective courses to enhance their knowledge in the preferred economics/finance domains. Electives include Alternative Investments and Distribution; Blockchain & Digital Economy; Continuous Time Financial Economics and Econometrics; High Frequency Trading; Machine Learning in Economics and Finance; Mathematics for Fixed Income and Derivative Securities; Portfolio Risk and Performance Analysis. Not all courses are offered every year. Course titles and content are subject to change, and new courses may be added from time to time.
**Open (1CU)**: Students may take one course from MSFE/MSE electives; or pre-approved electives from other SMU Masters programmes; or a minimum 10-week internship/capstone project. The Open component will expand to **2CU effective August 2026**.
**Postgraduate Professional Development course (1CU)**: Students are required to complete a series of full-day skills-based, developmental workshops or experiential components facilitated by SMU faculty and experienced trainers from various industries.
Full-time students are required to complete a **minimum 10-week internship during the April Term**. If unable to take a credit-bearing internship, students may seek approval from the Academic Director to arrange an equivalent replacement, such as a Capstone Project or electives. Students who have accumulated, or will have accumulated, two years of relevant work experience by their graduation date may be exempted from the internship requirement, subject to approval.
The FAQ states that the MSFE is a Masters Degree program at SMU by coursework / Professional Masters Program, and there are **no thesis requirements**. Students of the MSFE programme are required to complete **4 foundations, 6 core modules, 3 electives, 1 open and 1 Postgraduate Professional Development course**. There are two admission pathways: Accelerated Pathway and Regular Pathway. The Accelerated Pathway is for students with strong economics/finance knowledge and quantitative techniques who are exempted from foundation courses. The Regular Pathway is for students from other disciplines who do not have the necessary training in economics theory, finance and quantitative techniques. In order to graduate, students must complete **all 15 modules** and maintain an overall GPA of **2.5 and above**. All lessons and examinations are conducted in English for both pathways under the MSFE programme.

Cost of Attendance.content:
Living expenses will vary depending on your lifestyle and accommodation. However, the average international student would be able to stay within a monthly budget of **S$2000**. Estimated breakdown of basic living expenses:
| Item | Cost Per Month |
| --- | --- |
| **Accommodation** | **S$250 - S$800** |
| **Utilities** | **S$40 - S$100** |
| **Transportation** | **S$200** |
| **Telecommunications** | **S$50** |
| **Books & Stationery** | **S$200 per term** |
| **Personal Expenses (mobile phone, meals, etc)** | **S$100 - S$300** |
| **Food** | **S$300 - S$450** |

Financial Aid.content:
SOE MSFE Merit Scholarships
- **Benefits:** The Merit 2 Scholarship comprises a monetary award of **S$4,000 (inclusive of GST)**.
- **Eligibility criteria:** Outstanding applicants to the MSFE are eligible for the Merit Scholarships. The offer is conditional on matriculation into the MSFE, i.e., the scholarship awardee must matriculate into the programme in order for the scholarship to be disbursed. Deferment of studies beyond the financial year would render the scholarship award null and void.
- **Exclusions:** You must not be a concurrent recipient of any other SMU-funded scholarship.
- **Application Process:** All applicants are automatically considered for the scholarship; no additional application is required.
SOE MSFE Diversity Scholarships
- **Benefits:** The scholarship comprises a monetary award of **S$8,000 (inclusive of GST)**.
- **Eligibility criteria:** MSFE applicants with good academic backgrounds and who are citizens of countries that are underrepresented in the programme are eligible for the SOE MSE/MSFE Diversity Scholarship. The scholarship awardee must matriculate into the MSE/MSFE programme in order for the scholarship to be disbursed. Deferment of studies beyond the financial year would render the scholarship award null and void.
- **Exclusions:** You must not be a concurrent recipient of any other SMU-funded scholarship.
- **Application Process:** All eligible applicants are automatically considered for the scholarship; no additional application is required.
SMU ASEAN PG Scholarship
- **Benefits:** The scholarship comprises a monetary award of **S$10,000 (inclusive of GST)**.
- **Eligibility criteria:** The scholarship is open to citizens of ASEAN member countries or observer nations (PNG and Timor-Leste). Recipient must matriculate into the MSFE programme to receive the award. Deferment of studies beyond the financial year would render the scholarship award null and void.
- **Exclusions:** You must not be a concurrent recipient of any other SMU-funded scholarship.
- **Application Process:** All eligible applicants are automatically considered for the scholarship; no additional application is required.
MAS Prize in Economics
- **Benefits:** The scholarship comprises a certificate and monetary award of **S$2,000**.
- **Eligibility criteria:** Open to postgraduate students with a minimum cumulative GPA of **3.20 and above**. Must be full-time Singaporean or Permanent Resident student from the School of Economics.
Financing Options
- Scholarships and Outstanding Student Awards are available for deserving students.
- SkillsFuture Funding for Singapore Citizens. Click [here](https://www.skillsfuture.gov.sg/credit) for more details.
- Singapore Citizens aged 40 years and above are entitled to a SkillsFuture Credit (Mid-Career) top up of **$4,000** to offset the tuition fees. Click [here](https://www.skillsfuture.gov.sg/level-up-programme) for more details.
- Singapore Citizens with eligible Post Secondary Education Account (PSEA) may utilize balance funds for tuition fees. Click [here](https://www.moe.gov.sg/financial-matters/psea) for more details.
Discounts
- **Alumni Discount:** SMU and SUTD alumni are eligible for a **10% discount**.

Multiple Applications.content: If you have applied for more than one programme, you are only required to take the test once. Please contact your first-choice’s programme office to register for the test and update the other programme office upon the completion of your test via email to ensure timely processing of all your SMU applications.

Deferral Admission Policy.content:
- If students have to defer their studies due to unforeseen circumstances, they “will have to write in to seek permission from the Programme Office.”
- For SOE MSFE Merit Scholarships, “Deferment of studies beyond the financial year would render the scholarship award null and void.”
- For SOE MSFE Diversity Scholarships, “Deferment of studies beyond the financial year would render the scholarship award null and void.”
- For the SMU ASEAN PG Scholarship, “Deferment of studies beyond the financial year would render the scholarship award null and void.”
